name: Verdict invariant magnitude non monotone grid convergence MPM rigid body
goal: Diagnostic guidance for a coupled MPM rigid-vehicle/water simulation whose BINARY verdict is grid-invariant across g48/g64/g96 at three masses (identical realized depth to 7 dp, all nine runs same verdict) while the continuous observable is strongly NON-MONOTONE: final_disp_mag_m rises 87.8 percent g48->g64 then falls 59.2 percent g64->g96 at 1100 kg, and rises 22.3 then falls 50.3 at 1609 kg, with two measures of the same displacement inside one run disagreeing by 3.4 percent. Asks what to check and IN WHAT ORDER to separate a genuine solver defect from expected behaviour of an instantaneous transient quantity under refinement; whether GCI/Richardson can legitimately be applied to a non-monotone or non-asymptotic sequence; and the known interaction whereby refining at fixed particles-per-cell increases cell-crossing error and can destroy convergence.
summary: A GRID-INVARIANT STABILITY VERDICT DOES NOT ESTABLISH CONVERGENCE OF DISPLACEMENT. Transient end-point quantities can remain grid-dependent or oscillatory, while MPM particle quadrature, discontinuous basis gradients and grid crossing can destroy monotone spatial convergence [Sya17, Ste00, Bau23]. PRESCRIBED DIAGNOSTIC ORDER, four steps. (1) SEPARATE COUPLING FROM DISCRETIZATION FIRST. Audit discrete mass, momentum, angular momentum, energy and hydrostatic buoyancy; compare the velocity-average force against a wetted-surface traction or control-volume force. A persistent 25-30 percent force deficit is a COUPLING/MODEL-FORM error, NOT evidence of insufficient grid resolution [Hyd19, Nan17]. Test the rigid body in hydrostatics and in a prescribed-flow problem before returning to two-way coupling. (2) THEN ISOLATE MPM ERROR. Manufactured/analytic single-material tests; refine dt with h at fixed CFL; vary particle phase/offset and particles-per-cell; log particle crossings, quadrature imbalance, transfer error and energy drift. At FIXED particles-per-cell, smaller cells mean MORE crossings per physical trajectory, so error can INCREASE rather than converge [Ste00, Ber21c, Tra19b]. Compare GIMP, CPDI, B-spline, APIC/MLS variants [Bar04, Bau23]. (3) REMOVE TRANSIENT CONTAMINATION. Run substantially longer, identify a demonstrated stationary window, discard the initial transient, and converge time-averaged mean/RMS/spectral quantities, integrated force/impulse, or event times/threshold crossings, NOT one final displacement [Eca19, Ber21d, Sya17]. Check the verdict's margin from its decision threshold. (4) TREAT THREE NON-MONOTONE VALUES AS DIAGNOSTIC, NOT GCI DATA. Richardson/GCI assumes an asymptotic error model; non-asymptotic or oscillatory sequences require more grids and methods such as least-squares, bounded oscillatory estimates, or conservative factor-of-safety procedures [Phi14, Log05, Bro07b, Xin10].
